title_en: EU Green Agriculture Initiative in Armenia (EU-GAIA)
budget_original: EUR 9.7 million EU commitment (EC IATI record); total programme budget reported as EUR 11.7 million by news.am. UNDP-managed share in UNDP IATI record: USD 2.30 million.
cofinancing_note: EU funded, co-funded by Austrian Development Cooperation; ADA is the main implementing partner, UNDP implements Specific Objective 3 (herbs, legumes and sheep value chains).
summary_en: EU-GAIA aims at inclusive growth in the northern border marzes of Armenia (Shirak, Lori, Tavush) by boosting green agriculture and local added value. UNDP supports three value chains (herbs, legumes, sheep) while the Austrian Development Agency runs a grant scheme for green and organic agribusinesses (EUR 2.47 million call in 2020).
activities_en: Grant call for green and organic agribusinesses in Shirak, Lori and Tavush (fruit, berry and vegetable value chains; legumes, herbs and sheep breeding)
Demo sites: Sheep Genetic Centre (Azatan, Shirak), Herbs Seedling Centre and pedigree sheep farm with RFID weighing
Vegetable production, collection and packaging centre 'Lorva Hatik' in Stepanavan (Lori)
Training of farmers (sheep breeding, herb and legume cultivation, business planning with ICARE)
COVID-19 response package (EUR 456,500) with tractors, seedlings, inputs and post-harvest support
results_en: More than 350 beneficiaries trained and more than 400 French meat-breed sheep imported and distributed (UNDP report via FAO platform)
80 beneficiaries selected, 60 already equipped (FAO platform entry)
About 20 t of elite legume seed distributed, yielding more than 200 t of legume seed
'Lorva Hatik' centre: about 25 ha under cultivation with collaborating farmers in 2022

locations.evidence: Project activities concentrated in Shirak, Lori and Tavush regions (FAO Green Agriculture platform entry; IATI UNDP record lists Lori, Shirak, Tavush)
Same source: UNDP supports herbs, legumes and sheep value chains in Tavush, Lori and Shirak

Rural water supply for consumption and agricultural use, coordinated with water management companies

donors: Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC)

46,450 farmers earned more income; 396 off-farm jobs created
